description: The Settings dialog's Subscriptions page (Baude's, Record's and the phone's; on the phone the second page of Settings, switched to by the bar at its foot as the desktop dialog's switcher is when narrow): the Claude and Codex subscription accounts kept on the host picked beside New session (as ☰ → Terminal, Kubernetes… and Databases… use it), changed there through its accounts request. Named Subscriptions, not Providers: Settings' Meta group and the model pickers already call inference providers (Ollama, MLX, an endpoint) Providers.
opens: Settings… → Subscriptions (the dialog's page switcher; the phone's: the bar at Settings' foot)

parts.name: Host
parts.shows: Row "Host" with the picked host's name after it.

parts.name: provider group
parts.shows: For Claude, then Codex: a heading (the provider's logo and name), then a card for each subscription stacked, then a boxed list with Add account.

decisions.said: Baude needs to be able to support running claude with different subscriptions, e.g. a team sub for work and an ultra sub for home that they absolutely need to keep separate (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app (Baude, Record, the phone) lets you keep several named Claude and Codex accounts on each host, changed on the host picked beside New session, and pick each provider's default; a chat runs under the account its host's default was when it was made (or first written in) and keeps it when resumed or forked; a chat started from another on the same host (a fork, a side question, a subagent it spawns) runs under that chat's accounts; credentials never leave their host

decisions.said: The subscriptions page is structured wrong: the account picker and the usage are lumped together. Each subscription should be its own card, stacked, with its usage as bars with percentages below its name, read again automatically every 30 seconds; over the cards a pill whose dropdown picks the subscription used; and rename and remove under the dots on each card (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Subscriptions page shows, for each provider, a heading with a pill (the subscription a new chat on the host takes; its dropdown picks another), then one card per subscription stacked under it; each account's card has ⋮ (Rename…, Sign In Again… or Replace Token…, Remove…); each Claude card shows its own usage as a bar per limit with its name and percentage, read as the page is shown and every 30 seconds while it is, with no button to read it

decisions.said: (BaudeInternal#278, paraphrased) Current Subscription doesn't make sense once there's the provider override (a chat's provider picker): get rid of that field
decisions.rule: No app's Subscriptions page has a Current Subscription row or any other pick of a default subscription: a chat's provider picker is the one place a subscription is chosen. A new chat on a host takes the subscription a chat's provider picker last picked there for its model's provider (a Current Subscription picked before is kept as that pick), else the CLI's own sign-in, as one removed leaves it

parts.name: subscription card
parts.shows: One card per subscription, stacked: the provider's CLI default first (Claude's where the host has claude, Codex's where it has codex and says it reads Codex's usage: the accounts answer's codex_usage; an older host's Codex cards have no usage), then each account. Its name, and ⋮ on an account's card (CLI default has none). A Claude card then has its usage: for each limit, its name with its percentage at the end ("Five Hour Limit (Resets 3:16 PM)" … "25%"; "Weekly Limit (Resets Friday 3:16 PM)", or "Weekly Limit (Resets 3:16 PM)" where it resets today; the times in the viewer's local time and clock format) and a bar under them filled that far; till the page's own read answers, the host's last reading of it the same way but greyed (half opacity), and "Checking…" only where the host has none; "Usage unavailable for this sign-in" for a token account (a setup token can't read them) or the error if reading failed. A Codex card has its usage the same way, its limits as Codex's App Server says them (its five-hour and weekly windows named as Claude's); "Usage unavailable for this sign-in" where Codex says its sign-in isn't a ChatGPT plan's (an API key's, or none: its two authentication-required errors); "Sign in to this Codex profile again" for an account whose folder has no sign-in; "Could not read usage from Codex" for any other failure, a hang included, which leaves the host's last reading as it was.

actions.does: Menu: Rename…, Sign In Again… (Replace Token… for a token account), Remove…

Each card's usage is read from the host (accounts usage, its id; "" for Claude's CLI default, "" with provider codex for Codex's) as the page is shown and every 30 seconds while it's shown and the app (the phone's) or window (the desktop's) is in front, one read at a time per card, the bars drawn again in place; the host reads each account's usage once per ~25 s however many clients ask, one claude at a time and one codex at a time (a hung codex holds no claude's read) (Codex's: its App Server's account/rateLimits/read, asked without the reset-credit details, run with the subscription's CODEX_HOME, ~/.codex for CLI default); every answer to accounts carries the host's last reading of each subscription with when it was read (last_usage), which the page shows greyed till its own read of that card answers

decisions.said: There needs to be a way of seeing claude sub usage in the app
decisions.rule: Every app's Subscriptions page reads the default Claude account's usage when asked, and says "Usage unavailable for this sign-in" where its sign-in can't be asked (a setup token's has no profile scope)

decisions.said: The subscriptions page is structured wrong: the account picker and the usage are lumped together. Each subscription should be its own card, stacked, with its usage as bars with percentages below its name, read again automatically every 30 seconds; over the cards a pill whose dropdown picks the subscription used; and rename and remove under the dots on each card (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Subscriptions page shows, for each provider, a heading with a pill (the subscription a new chat on the host takes; its dropdown picks another), then one card per subscription stacked under it; each account's card has ⋮ (Rename…, Sign In Again… or Replace Token…, Remove…); each Claude card shows its own usage as a bar per limit with its name and percentage, read as the page is shown and every 30 seconds while it is, with no button to read it

decisions.said: 226 should be Five Hour Limit (Resets <TIME>) and Weekly Limit (Resets <DAY> <TIME>) or just <TIME> if the Weekly Reset Time is today.
decisions.rule: Every app labels a Claude card's limits Five Hour Limit (Resets <time>) and Weekly Limit (Resets <day> <time>), or Weekly Limit (Resets <time>) when the weekly reset is today, the times as the host's usage read says them, shown in the viewer's local time and clock format

decisions.said: The subscription percentages last read should be cached, and shown a bit grey while they're read again (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Subscriptions page shows each Claude card's usage as its host last read it, greyed, as soon as the page opens, until the page's own read answers with the current reading; the host keeps that last reading and when it was taken, so every app (and any later one) gets it from the host rather than keeping its own; "Checking…" shows only where the host has never read that subscription

decisions.said: (BaudeInternal#264, paraphrased) Codex's CLI default shows no usage amounts
decisions.rule: Every app's Subscriptions page has a card for Codex's CLI default where the host has codex, and every Codex card (CLI default and each account) shows its usage as a Claude card does: a bar per limit with its name, reset time and percentage, read the same way

parts.name: Add account
parts.shows: Button row "Add account" with a plus. Where the host lacks the provider's program (Codex's codex, by the host's deps), its Dependencies row in its place: "Codex CLI isn't installed", the install command with Copy (else the install page); Copy toasts "Copied: run it in a terminal", Settings having no Try Again.

decisions.said: Settings → Subscriptions showed a raw "No such file or directory: 'codex'" error; the dependencies page already has a central store that knows whether runtimes and dependencies are installed, and it should gate features like this one (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Subscriptions page asks the host's dependency store (schema/deps, the same one Settings → Dependencies lists) whether each provider's program is there; where it isn't, that provider's Add account row is replaced by its Dependencies row, titled "<program> isn't installed" with the host's install command and Copy (else its install page), and a sign-in the host is asked to run without it answers with that same line, never the run's OS error

parts.name: Add Claude account dialog
parts.shows: On a host with claude: heading "Add Claude account"; "Account name"; a two-way switcher, New login (picked) and Existing folder; under Existing folder only, "Signed-in Claude folder"; the accent button Sign in (Use signed-in folder under Existing folder); Close. Sign in runs claude auth login on the host with a new folder of the account's own, shown as the Claude sign-in card (the button gone, the fields and switcher greyed while it runs): "Signing in to Claude…" / dimmed "Starting the sign-in…" and Cancel; once the host has the page, "Open the sign-in page to sign in." (a link), a box "If the page shows a code, paste it here" with Continue (the accent button, usable once a code is typed), which passes the code to the login on the host, and under it, dimmed, "Checking the code…" then what claude says of it ("Invalid code…"); Cancel. The dialog closes once it's signed in; else the card says "Sign-in didn't finish" / dimmed why, with Try Again (the accent button) and the fields usable again; picking the other tab then lets go of the card and puts the dialog's own button back. Cancel stops it and gives back the fields and button; Close stops it. On a host without claude: "Account name", a password entry whose placeholder is "Paste the token from claude setup-token", Save account, Close.

decisions.said: claude auth login with a profile dir should pre preferred over oauth. similar to how we fall back to agent forwarding if we can't do provider forwarding (or vice versa). oauth token login should be used for things such as mobile where we can't guarantee the claude code binary.
decisions.rule: Every app adds a Claude account on a host that has claude as a config folder of its own there (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), signed in to with claude auth login run by that host with the folder: the host passes the sign-in page's link to the app (any device opens it) and the code the page shows is pasted back in the app and fed to the login; the host keeps only the folder, no token, and the account's chats run claude with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to it. An existing signed-in folder on the host can be used instead. A token from claude setup-token is the fallback, used only where claude can't be guaranteed: a host without claude, and the phone as a host

parts.name: Add Codex account dialog
parts.shows: Heading "Add Codex account"; "Account name"; a two-way switcher, New login (picked) and Existing folder; under Existing folder only, "Signed-in CODEX_HOME"; the accent button Sign in (Use signed-in profile under Existing folder); Close. Sign in runs codex login on the host with a new CODEX_HOME of the account's own (the browser's sign-in; the device code's on "Use a device code instead", or by itself where the browser's can't listen), shown as the Codex sign-in card, the fields and switcher greyed while it runs; the account is added once it's signed in. Close stops it.

parts.name: Codex sign-in card
parts.shows: In the dialog, under its fields, once Sign in is pressed (the dialog's own button gone while it's there): the card a chat's Sign in card is (LoginCard's: warning-bordered, a bold title, a line, then what can be done now), drawn from the sign-in's state as the host says it (accounts sign_in's login, a ChatLogin). The browser's, by default (codex login): waiting, "Signing in to Codex…" / dimmed "Starting the sign-in…"; once codex has said its page, the page's link as Claude's card has it: where the host is this machine's, the page opened in its browser at once (by codex itself on macOS, else by the app) and "A browser window should have opened to sign in. If it didn't, open the sign-in page."; another machine's and the phone's, "Open the sign-in page to sign in." and a box "Paste the address the browser ended on" with Continue (the accent button, usable once an address is typed, and not while "Checking the address…" shows) (that address passed to the host, which asks codex's server on its own 127.0.0.1 for it; "Checking the address…", then why not, dimmed, if it wasn't taken). On Baude and Record, for another machine's host, this machine's 127.0.0.1 at the port codex took (1455, else 1457) is passed on to the host the same way while it runs, so the browser's own way back reaches it and nothing need be pasted (where that port's taken here, the box is the way). Under it, "Use a device code instead" and Cancel. The device code's (codex login --device-auth: on that button, or by itself where codex can't listen on either port): waiting, dimmed "Requesting a device code…"; then its page's link the same way, the one-time code large (bold monospace, .device-code: 1.8em; the phone's 26 px), selectable, with Copy (the accent button) beside it ("Code copied" once pressed), and Cancel. Signed in: "Signed in to Codex" / "as <email>" (the email its sign-in names; else the account's name); the dialog stays till Close. Failed: "Sign-in didn't finish" / dimmed what codex said last (an error line, else "The Codex CLI did not complete sign-in"), and Try Again (the browser's again), with "Use a device code instead" where the browser's failed; the fields can be changed again first.

actions.does: Opens the sign-in page in this device's browser (on the host's own machine it's opened already, once, as the code comes)
Puts the code on the clipboard; the button says "Code copied"

actions.by: paste the address and click Continue (or press Enter)
actions.does: Passes the address the browser ended on to the host's sign-in, which requests it of codex's server on the host's 127.0.0.1; codex finishes, and the card says signed in or failed

actions.by: click Use a device code instead
actions.does: Stops the browser's sign-in and starts codex login --device-auth in its place
Lets go of the sign-in's connection, which stops codex login on the host (a new account's folder removed); the card goes and the dialog's fields and button come back
Signs in again as the dialog's button would (with a signed-in CODEX_HOME typed by then, that's added instead)

decisions.said: (BaudeInternal#262, paraphrased) the Codex device-code sign-in is poor next to Claude's: its link can't even be clicked
decisions.rule: Every app shows a Codex device-code sign-in as a card the way it shows a chat's Claude sign-in: drawn from its state as the host says it (signing in, signed in, failed with codex's reason; never codex's raw output), the sign-in page as a link that can be clicked (opened at once in the browser where the host is the app's own machine), the one-time code large with Copy, and Cancel

decisions.said: Device code honestly seems like the "oauth-token" like approach, somethign to fallback to but not default
decisions.rule: A Codex sign-in is codex login's browser sign-in by default, as Claude's is claude auth login; the device code (a beta that has to be switched on in ChatGPT's security settings) is the fallback: "Use a device code instead" in the card, and by itself where the browser's can't listen. For a host on another machine, the browser's way back to codex's 127.0.0.1 is passed on to the host: by this machine's own 127.0.0.1 where it can, else by pasting the address the browser ended on

parts.name: Rename dialog
parts.shows: Heading "Rename <name>", the name to edit, Rename, Close.

parts.name: Replace Token dialog
parts.shows: A token account's: heading "Replace the token for <name>", the token's password entry (its placeholder the setup-token line), Save, Close.

parts.name: Sign In Again dialog
parts.shows: Heading "Sign in to <name> again". A Claude folder account's: Sign in, then the Claude sign-in card, as Add Claude account's. Codex's: Sign in, then the Codex sign-in card (Add Codex account's), or, where the host lacks codex, its Dependencies row ("Codex CLI isn't installed", the install command with Copy) in place of the button. Close.

parts.name: Remove dialog
parts.shows: Heading "Remove <name>?", Cancel and Remove (destructive). Chats made under it say the account is gone when they next start.

states.name: loading
states.shows: The pills, cards and Add account only once the host answers.

states.name: host unreachable
states.shows: Each group holds the error the reach gave, with no pill.

states.name: phone picked beside New session
states.shows: Only computer hosts keep accounts: the page opens on the first computer host (the Host row names it), or, with none connected, the Host row reads "Not connected to a host process" with no groups.

decisions.rule: Every app's Subscriptions page shows each Claude subscription's usage on its card, read by itself (see BaudeInternal#226's decision), and says "Usage unavailable for this sign-in" where its sign-in can't be asked (a setup token's has no profile scope)

decisions.said: ChatGPT started work on a providers screen to separate work and personal accounts (the owner's request to finish it; review: a chat's account must be visible)
decisions.rule: Every app shows the account a chat runs under: its status bar host tooltip ("Account: <name>"), Copy Transcript's header ("Account"), Meta's list of chats; a sign-in card in a chat under a Claude account signs in to that account (a folder account's: claude auth login with its folder; a token account's: its token replaced), never the CLI's own sign-in; Meta's card signs in to the account Meta runs under

decisions.said: (coordinator, from the review) put all copy in schema/copy; the setup-token line becomes the entry's placeholder; no subtext
decisions.rule: Every app takes the page's wording from schema/copy/subscriptions.json; no row subtitles

decisions.said: (coordinator, from the owner's rule that only the owner decides overrides) the phone's Settings row in place of the page switcher was an agent's override
decisions.rule: Every app reaches Subscriptions as Settings' second page through the same page switcher (General, Subscriptions; on a narrow screen, the bar at the foot); no app opens it from a row

decisions.said: (review of PR 423, the coordinator's decision) claude won't write a user setting through a linked settings.json; the owner hates windows popping up
decisions.rule: Every app's Claude folder account made on a host links the host's Claude folder's projects, CLAUDE.md, commands, agents, skills, plugins, hooks and output-styles into the account's folder, and copies, as the folder is made, the host's settings.json and its user MCP servers (~/.claude.json's mcpServers) into the folder's own settings.json and .claude.json (each account's settings are then its own, as a Codex account's are); claude auth login run by a host opens no browser there (BROWSER is a no-op): the app shows the page's link

decisions.said: The subscriptions page is structured wrong: the account picker and the usage are lumped together. Each subscription should be its own card, stacked, with its usage as bars with percentages below its name, read again automatically every 30 seconds; over the cards a pill whose dropdown picks the subscription used; and rename and remove under the dots on each card (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Subscriptions page shows, for each provider, a heading with a pill (the subscription a new chat on the host takes; its dropdown picks another), then one card per subscription stacked under it; each account's card has ⋮ (Rename…, Sign In Again… or Replace Token…, Remove…); each Claude card shows its own usage as a bar per limit with its name and percentage, read as the page is shown and every 30 seconds while it is, with no button to read it

decisions.said: (BaudeInternal#279, paraphrased) Claude's sign-in shows Send beside Sign In, which is redundant; once sign-in has started, Sign In should give way to the next step (Continue, the accent button, where a code is needed), as Codex's does; both sign-in flows should make sense
decisions.rule: Every app's Claude and Codex sign-ins (Add account, Sign In Again, and a chat's Sign in card) go one step at a time, the same shape for both: the dialog's own button (Sign in, or Use signed-in folder/profile) goes once sign-in starts, and the sign-in shows as a card (a bold title, a line, then what can be done now). At each step at most one button is the accent one, labelled for what it does next: Continue beside the code box (Claude, shown once the page's link is) or the address box (Codex), usable once something is typed and not while what was sent is checked; Copy beside a device code; Try Again once it failed; changing New login / Existing folder after a failure puts the dialog's own button back in its place. No two buttons do the same thing; Cancel, Use a device code instead and Close are never the accent one. While the sign-in only waits on the browser, no button is the accent one

decisions.said: (BaudeInternal#279, paraphrased) the existing folder path box is always shown though it's rarely filled in; a tab-like choice between New login and an existing folder would be better
decisions.rule: Every app's Add account dialog (Claude's on a host with claude, and Codex's) puts a two-way switcher under the account name: New login (first, picked when it opens) and Existing folder; the folder's path box shows only under Existing folder, and the dialog's button says Sign in or Use signed-in folder/profile to match; with Existing folder picked and its box empty, the button focuses the box

removed.name: Current Subscription row in Settings → Subscriptions
removed.why: The owner (BaudeInternal#278, paraphrased): Current Subscription doesn't make sense once there's the provider override; get rid of that field. A chat's provider picker chooses its subscription, and new chats take its last pick
